sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
மதுசூதனன் மனோகரி மார ஜனனீ
மதுரவதனி மஹாலக்ஷ்மி மாதே
sections.translit:
madhusUdhanan manOgari mAra jananI
madhuravadhani mahAlakshmi mAthE
sections.en: Dear mother Mahalakshmi, you are the darling of Vishnu (Madhusudhanan). The god of love, Manmatha, is your son. Your face is as sweet as nectar.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
மனதினில் மகிழ்வும் மாசறு நினைவும்
மங்கா வளமும் மாண்பும் வழங்கிடும்
sections.translit:
manadhinil magizhvum mAsaRu ninaivum
mangA vaLamum mANbum vazhangidum
sections.en: You offer happiness to my mind and a thought process free of imperfections. You offer an immutable treasure, a source of enduring greatness and repute.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
மதியும் மாவலியும் துணையாய் மதம் நிறை மூகனை
மாய்த்தவள் நீயே மாரி போல மாநிதியொடு
மங்களமருளிடும் மலர்மகளே மகேஸ்வரி
மூடனெந்தன் மறுமை நீக்கி மேன்மை தருவாய்
sections.translit:
madhiyum mAvaliyum thuNaiyAy madham niRai mUkanai
mAytthavaL nIyE mAri pOla mAnidhiyodu
mangaLamaruLidum malarmagaLE magEswari
mUdanendhan maRumai nIkki mEnmai tharuvAy
sections.en: Oh Supreme Goddess seated on a lotus flower, you used your intellect and strength to annihilate the ego-centered demon Mookasura. Like rain, you offer prosperity and auspiciousness to devotees. Please remove this ignorant soul’s birth cycle and offer salvation.

notes: Lines 1 and 2 of the charanam describe the Goddess Mookambika who caused the death of the evil demon, Kamasura (Mookasura) domiciled in a huge temple in Kollur, Karnataka near Mangalore. There, the deity is visited by large crowds each day. Per ancient legend, from his guru, Sukhracharya , a demon named Kamasura got wind of his imminent death at the hands of a woman. He performed severe penance to obtain immortality from Lord Siva. Pleased by his austerity, Siva appeared before him. Apprehensive of the outcome, Adiparasakthi (a blend of Goddess Mahalakshmi, Saraswathi, and Parvathy) blocked the boon by taking away the demon’s ability to speak. Thus, Kamasura could not ask for what he wanted from Siva and became Mookasura (a demon without speech). The deity eventually killed him and relieved the devas, and the entire universe, from the demon’s atrocities. For more reading, see: Story of Goddess Mookambika Mookambika Temple At Kollur When Goddess Saraswathi took away Mookasura’s ability to speak, she left him with only his ego. Humiliated but unbroken in spirit, the asura faced off with her. He fell at last before the Supreme Goddess, who, together with her two divine co-equals, delivered a final blow. For details, see: Goddess Lakshmi as Adi Parasakthi kills Mookasura
